newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - SGS-Thomson drops in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - SGS-Thomson drops in New York.

text.p: New York shares of Franco-Italian chipmaker SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV tumbled on Wednesday, hit by its warning about profits in the first quarter of 1997.
Thomson's drop highlighted trade in foreign shares and American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) as the Dow industrials fell on a selloff in International Business Machines Corp stock.
"The world's kind of mesmerized by IBM today," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.

Thomson shares dropped 11 dollars, or 14 percent, to 68-1/4 in very heavy volume after president and chief executive Pasquale Pistorio said the first quarter of 1997 had "less order visibility" than usual.
He added that the period's revenues would be close to those of 1996's third quarter.
Among other European shares, Britain's Vodafone Group Plc rose 1-7/8 to 45-5/8 on buoyant subscriber figures and ahead of a February presentation to U.S. analysts and investors.

European stocks such as British Airways and British Petroleum Co Plc, which have several shares for each ADR, were weighed by the strengthening dollar. British Airways was off 1-1/2 to 97-7/8, and British Petroleum dropped 5/8 to 144-1/4.

Latin American shares mostly were off slightly, reflecting declines in their home stock markets. Chile's Empresa Nacional de Electridad S.A., or Endesa, fell 3/4 to 17-7/8 amid a peso revaluation against the dollar.
"The effort didn't seem to be too well received" by foreign investors, a trader said.
Decliners led advancers by 263 to 205 among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 31 million shres in late morning.
